title: OKRs-to-Roadmap Translation and Quarterly Gating Framework
creator: Maya Patel
description: Create a repeatable framework that translates company-level OKRs into prioritized quarterly roadmap commitments with clear decision gates. Deliver a one-page translation template, a quarterly gating checklist for PMs and Eng leads, and a rollout plan for the org-wide cadence. The framework should enable leadership to: (1) identify initiatives that materially move key results, (2) set minimal viable success criteria for each initiative, and (3) gate scope or de-scope features based on measurable progress at mid-quarter checkpoints.
acceptance_criteria: One-page OKR->Roadmap translation template published in Confluence with example for each company OKR.
Quarterly gating checklist (Go/Adjust/Stop) documented and adopted by at least 4 cross-functional teams for the pilot quarter.
Ship two dashboards: an initiative-level progress dashboard (OKR-aligned metrics) and a risk heatmap surfaced in the Console for exec review.
Run a 90-minute training + Q&A for PMs and Eng managers; collect feedback and iterate before company rollout.
Document post-pilot retrospective with recommended updates to the framework and sign-off from Head of Product and VP Eng.
comments: 2026-02-16 Maya Patel: Kickoff meeting with Eng, Design, and Finance. Agreed scope: pilot with GPT Serving, Console, and Dedicated teams. Action: draft template by 02/22.

2026-02-22 Ethan Rivera: Posted initial translation template to Confluence. Included fields: OKR, hypothesis, primary metric, secondary metric, minimal success criteria, dependencies, known risks, and gating cadence.

2026-02-26 Priya Singh (Design): Provided feedback on template UX—recommend simplifying metrics section and adding a consumer-level success story example. Marked two fields as optional for early-stage initiatives.
2026-03-02 Liam O'Connor (Eng): Flagged risk: we need standardized telemetry for some KR metrics. Created ENG-8292 to instrument missing metrics; dependency noted here.

2026-03-05 Ethan Rivera: Drafted quarterly gating checklist. Trade-offs discussed: tight gates reduce scope churn but risk delaying critical infra work. Decided to include an engineering buffer lane for platform upgrades.

2026-03-08 Maya Patel: Ran pilot orientation with four teams. Initial pushback on mandatory Go/Adjust/Stop meetings cadence—agreed to reduce frequency for low-risk initiatives. Updated checklist accordingly.
2026-03-11 Ana Morales (Finance): Requested explicit cost/run-rate signal in the template for Dedicated commitments—added 'expected monthly run-rate' field.
2026-03-12 Ethan Rivera: Linking pilot sub-issues and scheduling training session for 2026-03-22. Next: finalize dashboards and confirm instrumentation completion.
notes: Decision log: Use three-tier gate outcomes (Go / Adjust / Stop) with quantitative thresholds where possible; qualitative review allowed for early research spikes.
Trade-offs: Prioritization will prefer initiatives with clear KR impact and low operational entropy. Platform work may be put into a buffer lane to avoid unnecessary stops for infra maintenance.
Rollout plan: pilot quarter -> retro -> adapt -> Q3 org-wide adoption if pilot meets >70% adoption and leadership sign-off.
